signal: PBR-1 agitator gearbox vibration climbing at constant speed
aiInterpretation: Gearbox vibration on PBR-1's agitator has more than doubled since about 09:20 while speed stayed at 48 rpm, and the mechanical seal is running warmer. PBR-2's identical drive is flat. The batch has one day left before harvest.

detail.signal: Gearbox vibration 4.5 mm/s at 14:05, up from 1.9 at 09:20 (alert 4.5, alarm 7.1). Seal temperature 44 → 52 °C.
detail.observed: Agitator speed steady at 48 rpm; power up slightly (14.2 → 14.68 kW). DO, pH and temperature control normal. PBR-2's gearbox, same model, reads 1.7 mm/s.
detail.derived: Vibration, seal temperature and power are rising together at unchanged speed, so it is the drive, not the process. The rise is accelerating: 0.9 mm/s in the last hour, which would reach the 7.1 alarm in about 3 hours if it continues.
detail.inferred: Possible gearbox bearing wear or lubrication loss, with heat reaching the bottom-mounted mechanical seal. Not yet confirmed.
detail.recommendation: Take a portable vibration spectrum and check gearbox oil level and seal barrier condensate. Do not stop the agitator mid-batch; agree a plan with MS&T to reach tomorrow's 08:00 harvest, or harvest early if the seal barrier pressure drops.

relatedOccurrences.summary: PBR-3 agitator gearbox bearing replaced at turnaround after a slow vibration rise over one batch.

detail.whatChangedSummary: No speed, setpoint or maintenance change on PBR-1 today.

detail.confidence: Three related signals agree; cause not yet confirmed
detail.risk: Medium — a seal failure mid-batch is a sterility breach and loses ~64 kg of antibody
detail.expectedOutcome: Batch reaches harvest; gearbox inspected at turnaround

signal: SBR-1 DO probe B jumping — probe A, O₂ flow and cells all say otherwise
aiInterpretation: The seed bioreactor's monitoring DO probe swung between 14% and 64% for an hour. Control probe A held 40%, the O₂ sparge never moved and the culture kept growing, so the process was fine: a loose probe cable connector.

detail.signal: DO probe B read between 14% and 64% from 09:35 to 10:40; probe A stayed between 39.5% and 40.7%.
detail.observed: O₂ sparge flow varied by only 0.6 slpm over the window; pCO₂, pH and viable cell density on trend. Probe B's own signal-quality index fell to 57 (normal ~96).
detail.derived: A real DO swing of that size would move the DO cascade and both probes together. Only one probe moved, and its diagnostic dropped with it — an instrument fault, not the culture.
detail.inferred: Intermittent connection in the probe B cable; confirmed when the connector was found loose.
detail.recommendation: Record the probe B excursion in the batch record as an instrument event (no process impact); check the connector strain relief before the next SIP.
detail.whatChangedSummary: Instrument technician reseated the probe B connector at 10:40; readings normal from 10:45.

signal: PBR-3 SIP failed on the drain cold point — the cause was the clean steam supply
aiInterpretation: PBR-3's first sterilization never got its drain thermocouple to 121.1 °C and was aborted. The vessel was fine: the clean steam header had sagged from 3.0 to about 1.7 bar(g) because CSG-1's feed pump was cavitating. After the strainer was cleaned the second SIP passed.

detail.signal: Drain (cold point) temperature peaked at 115.5 °C at 10:40 during SIP #1 (target ≥ 121.1 °C for the hold); vessel reached 119.5 °C.
detail.observed: CSG-1 generator level began hunting between 42% and 69% at 10:10; header pressure fell to 1.66 bar(g) from 10:20; vessel pressure dropped from 1.10 to 0.92 bar(g) at the same time. Steam traps on PBR-3 checked OK.
detail.derived: The steam supply problem started 10–20 minutes before the cold spot and explains it: lower steam pressure means a lower saturation temperature and slower purging of air and condensate from the drain leg.
detail.inferred: Clean steam generator feed pump cavitation (blocked suction strainer); confirmed when the strainer was cleaned at 11:10.
detail.recommendation: Close the deviation with CSG-1 as root cause; add the feed-pump strainer to the CSG-1 PM route. PBR-3 SIP #2 passed and can proceed to the pressure hold.

signal: CAP-1 stopped mid-load — guard filter pressure high-high
aiInterpretation: The Protein A skid shut its feed pump during cycle 2 when the guard filter in front of the column hit its 2.5 bar interlock. The column itself was fine. The filter was replaced and the load resumed after 45 minutes, inside the validated 4-hour load hold.

detail.signal: Skid flow went from 26 L/min (second stage of the dual-flow load) to 0 at 09:55; guard filter DP rose from 0.35 bar at 09:30 to 2.18 bar at 09:50.
detail.observed: 1,278 L of cycle 2 load was on the column when it stopped. Column DP normal before and after; after the filter change the guard filter read 0.30 bar at full flow.
detail.derived: Only the guard filter DP rose, and fast (minutes, not cycles) — a filter plugging with fines, not column fouling or a compressed bed.
detail.inferred: Guard filter plugged by fines in the clarified harvest; the harvest hold tank sample showed higher-than-usual turbidity (27 NTU vs < 10).
detail.recommendation: Record the interruption and the hold time in the batch record; send the used filter and a harvest sample to QC; ask MS&T to review HRV-1 depth-filter performance before tomorrow's harvest.
detail.whatChangedSummary: Guard filter replaced 10:35; cycle 2 load resumed at 10:40 and completed; cycles 3–5 ran normally.

whatChanged.description: CAP-1 guard filter DP high-high — feed pump interlock.

Cycle 2 load resumed.

detail.confidence: Confirmed — DP normal on the new filter
detail.risk: Low — resumed well inside the hold time; about 50 minutes lost on the purification schedule
detail.expectedOutcome: Cycles 3–8 on the new filter; QC result on the filter and harvest sample

signal: Protein A cycles on schedule — but more antibody is going out with the flow-through each cycle
aiInterpretation: Every CAP-1 cycle today has loaded the same volume on time, so the purification plan looks on track. But the flow-through breakthrough at the end of each load has risen from about 1% to over 4%, and the step yield has fallen with it.

detail.signal: End-of-load breakthrough: 1.1% → 2.0% → 3.1% → 4.6% (cycles 1–4); cycle 5 is already at 4.6% with a sample still to go.
detail.observed: Step yield 95.3% → 94.4% → 93.0% → 91.4%. Load volume, flow and residence time are identical every cycle; column DP unchanged (1.34 vs 1.35 bar). Resin is on cycle 191 of its 200-cycle validated lifetime.
detail.derived: The headline (volume processed, cycles on time) hides a loss of about 0.5 kg of antibody over cycles 2–4 compared with cycle 1. The trend is cycle-over-cycle, not a one-off, and the guard-filter event (PSIT04) does not explain cycles 3 and 4.
detail.inferred: Possible loss of dynamic binding capacity (resin near end of life, or incomplete regeneration), or a higher harvest titer than the load volume assumes. Not yet confirmed.
detail.recommendation: Ask QC for a rush titer on the cycle 4 flow-through and the harvest pool; if capacity is down, reduce load per cycle for cycles 6–8 per the batch record's load-challenge range and bring forward the column repack.

signal: AHU-3 lost its supply fan — post-viral suite pressures collapsed and POL-1 was stopped
aiInterpretation: AHU-3's duty fan tripped on a drive fault at 12:10. Room pressures in the post-viral suite fell to near zero and the airlock reversed, so POL-1 was put on hold. The standby fan was started at 12:22 and pressures recovered by 12:30.

detail.signal: Supply airflow fell from 18,488 to 1,190 m³/h at 12:10. Chromatography room DP 15.3 → 1.1 Pa; airlock AL-7 reversed to -1.3 Pa.
detail.observed: Room temperature peaked at 21.3 °C. POL-1 on hold 12:10–12:50 (about 1,200 L of load deferred). Room DPs back above 5 Pa at 12:30.
detail.derived: One cause (the fan) produced every downstream symptom in order: airflow, then room pressures, then the processing hold. UF/DF CIP and the DS freezer were not affected.
detail.inferred: Fan A variable-speed drive tripped on overcurrent; drive fault log confirms.
detail.recommendation: Keep Fan B on duty. Wait for the post-excursion EM plates (read at 48–72 h) before dispositioning POL-1's hold; raise a work order on the Fan A drive.
detail.whatChangedSummary: Standby Fan B started 12:22; pressures normal from 12:30; POL-1 resumed 12:50 after a room clearance check. EM results pending.

signal: PBR-2 dissolved CO₂ building up — past its normal range and heading for the proven acceptable limit
aiInterpretation: pCO₂ in PBR-2 has risen steadily since about 10:15 and left its normal operating range (≤ 120 mmHg) at 12:20. The pH has sunk to the bottom of its dead band, the pH loop has all but stopped sparging CO₂ and is pumping more base, and osmolality is creeping up. At this rate pCO₂ reaches the 160 mmHg PAR limit around 15:05.

detail.signal: pCO₂ 146 mmHg at 14:05, up from 90 at 10:15; rising about 13 mmHg/h (NOR ≤ 120, PAR ≤ 160).
detail.observed: Culture pH 7.00 → 6.93; CO₂ sparge 13 → 2 slpm; base pump 26 → 63 mL/min; osmolality 357 → 361 mOsm/kg; off-gas CO₂ 5.3 → 8.5%. VCD 22.1 ×10⁶/mL (near peak). DO steady at 40%. PBR-1 pCO₂ steady at 86 mmHg.
detail.derived: CO₂ is being produced faster than it is being stripped. The pH loop is already doing what it can (CO₂ sparge almost off); the extra base it adds raises osmolality, so waiting makes two CPPs worse.
detail.inferred: Hypotheses: reduced CO₂ stripping (headspace overlay or sparge air lower than the recipe), or higher CO₂ production at peak cell density. Not yet diagnosed.
detail.recommendation: Check the overlay and air-sparge flows against the day-7 recipe values and restore them if they differ; if pCO₂ is still rising in 30 minutes, raise air sparge within its NOR per SOP. Take an offline blood-gas sample to confirm the probe. Notify QA of the NOR excursion.
